clue.text: Golden farthing provided small change for tithe

parts.note: F is the old abbreviation for a farthing, a quarter of a pre-decimal penny
if means provided, as in 'provided that'

indicators.note: a small change to the word tithe is a slight reshuffle of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tossing a gold farthing into the collection to cover their church tithe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' reads as coins, but it signals rearranging TITHE into TIETH. A golden anniversary is the fiftieth.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden wedding or jubilee marks the fiftieth year, so golden stands for that ordinal anniversary.

clue.text: Very unfriendly back home on the farm

parts.note: fro means back, as in to and fro
a sty is a pig's home on a farm

explanation.surface: Someone returning home to the farm and getting a cold welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A frosty manner is icy and cold, so it describes someone very unwelcoming.

clue.text: Visionary pop star out of Arkansas

parts.note: Fanta is a brand of fizzy pop

indicators.note: out of means those letters leave the word star

parts.note: taken as written
AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: A dreamy pop star leaving Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop star' reads as a singer; 'pop' is the soft drink FANTA and STAR loses AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantast is a dreamer who lives in fantasy, a visionary in the impractical sense.

clue.text: Amazing finch grew odd ribs and flew without wings

indicators.note: without wings means each word loses its outer letters, as a bird would lose its wings either side

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A freakish finch growing odd ribs and flying without wings would be remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without wings' applies to all five words: drop the first and last letters of finch, grew, odd, ribs and flew.
explanation.definitionFit: Incredible means hard to believe, so something astonishing or amazing.

clue.text: Absolute thug punches even if on his last legs

indicators.note: punches means the thug word breaks into the gap between the other two pieces

parts.note: tho is the informal spelling of though, meaning even if
going means dying, on the way out
a rough is a violent hooligan or thug

explanation.surface: A thug still throwing punches even when on his last legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punches' reads as the thug's blows, but it means the thug breaks into the other two pieces; 'tho' is the informal spelling of though.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughgoing means complete or utter, so it is a synonym for absolute.

clue.text: Artist quietly fills one with optimism

indicators.note: fills means the soft letter goes into the middle of the word for an optimist

parts.note: a hoper is a person who hopes
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A painter gently filling someone with hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Hopper was the American painter of Nighthawks.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Hopper was a celebrated American realist painter, so his surname names an artist.

clue.text: River flow that's sluggish, you'd say

indicators.note: you'd say means the word is as it would be spoken aloud

parts.note: to ooze is to flow slowly

explanation.surface: A river whose current is notably slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the Yorkshire Ouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a river in England, flowing through York, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Leading empire corrupted Republican

indicators.note: corrupted means the letters of empire are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dominant empire corrupted by a Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier means first or foremost, so a leading club is a premier one.

clue.text: Spooner's stockings get torn going for fruit on thorny bush

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, after Rev. Spooner

parts.note: hose are stockings
rips means gets torn

explanation.surface: Stockings snag and tear on a thorny bush.
explanation.walkthrough: HOSE RIPS with initial sounds swapped becomes ROSE HIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose hips are the red fruits of the rose, a prickly shrub.

clue.text: Have opening of present delayed

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of the word for present
delayed means that first letter is pushed back to arrive at the end instead

parts.note: now means at present, the present time

explanation.surface: Someone holding back from unwrapping a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means NOW; its opening N is delayed to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have or possess it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Clips of actor occupying a hundred stages

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: occupying means the actor and the short of sit inside the hundred and the stages

parts.note: legs are stages of a journey or race
O is a short form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp
thesp is short for thespian, an actor

explanation.surface: Film clips of one actor appearing on a hundred different stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clips' suggests film excerpts but is the definition; 'of' gives O, as in John o' Groats, going in with THESP.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes pegs are clips that fasten laundry to a washing line, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Celebrity had no soul, he rehashed Sam & Dave in the end

indicators.note: rehashed means the letters are reworked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: in the end picks the final letter of each of the two names

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that a singer with no soul reworked a Sam & Dave song.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam & Dave were a 1960s soul duo; the last letters M and E join the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A household name is someone so famous everyone knows them, so a celebrity.

clue.text: René's Cycle Among Nomadic Tuareg?

indicators.note: among means the French bike goes inside the rearranged letters
nomadic means wandering, so the letters of Tuareg wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
vélo is French for bicycle, and René is a typical Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman cycling among the desert-roaming Tuareg people, perhaps as a travel film.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a picture of the answer: a Frenchman's account of cycling among the Tuareg would be just that.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelogue is a film or book describing a journey, as a cyclist's account of the Sahara would be.

clue.text: A slice of beef is highly inappropriate food for vegetarian

indicators.note: A slice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Serving a vegetarian a slice of beef is highly inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetarians eat no animal flesh, and many exclude seafood too, so this food is wrong for them.

clue.text: Warning siren worried guards back to tag immigrants

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout

indicators.note: guards means the rearranged siren letters enclose that letter
worried means the letters of siren are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back to points to the last letter of tag

explanation.surface: A warning siren sounds as guards move to tag arriving immigrants.
explanation.walkthrough: SIREN rearranged gives INERS, which guards G, the back of tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreigners are people from another country, as immigrants are.

clue.text: Thread stitching wounds without us?

indicators.note: without means those letters are dropped from the stitching word

parts.note: suturing is the stitching of wounds
us read as the plural of the letter U: two Us

explanation.surface: A medic wondering whether wounds could be stitched without help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is read as two letter Us, both removed from SUTURING.
explanation.definitionFit: String is a cord or twine, a thicker kind of thread, so the nouns match.

clue.text: European received simple epitaph, perhaps writing his own eulogy?

parts.note: got means received
RIP, rest in peace, is the simplest epitaph on a gravestone

explanation.surface: A European whose gravestone reads plainly, though he wrote his own glowing eulogy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: praising yourself at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Composing praise of oneself is an act of vanity, an indulgence in self-importance.

clue.text: Very unpopular journalist has pissed off in the van

indicators.note: in the van means at the front, so the rearranged letters lead and the journalist follows
off means the letters of pissed are gone wrong, in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A drunk journalist sent off in the van, much disliked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is the front, as in vanguard, so the rearranged letters come before ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be despised is to be loathed and scorned, which is being very unpopular.

clue.text: Old gunfighter to carry a silencer

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the Wild West lawman of the OK Corral gunfight
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A Wild West gunman carrying a silencer on his pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silencer' suggests a gun attachment, but here it blocks sound for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug shuts out noise from the ear, so it acts as a personal sound blocker.

clue.text: Taking soldiers miles round after stretching?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers
a round shape stretched becomes an oval

explanation.surface: Soldiers taking a round of miles after stretching before a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A removal is a taking away of something, so the nouns overlap.

clue.text: Stuff dug up by university that promises repercussions

parts.note: ore is mineral rock dug up in mining
LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London

explanation.surface: Something unearthed by a university that threatens consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a threat ending, as in 'pay up, or else'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is tacked onto a demand to warn of unpleasant consequences, a threat of punishment.

clue.text: That was a silly mistake, on reflection, retaining clumsy cleaner

indicators.note: retaining means the reversed exclamation holds the clumsy word inside
on reflection means the exclamation is read as in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: oops is said after a silly mistake
ham means clumsy, as in ham-fisted

explanation.surface: Clumsily spilling a cleaning product, with an admission of the slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' as clumsy comes from ham-fisted; the exclamation is the whole phrase 'That was a silly mistake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap for washing hair or carpets, so it is a cleaning agent.

clue.text: Briny issue, maybe salt

parts.note: the briny is the sea
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the sea's product is salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks salt as one example of the verb: to season food.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it, and salting is one way of doing that.

clue.text: Hunter returning in the morning in good spirits

indicators.note: returning means the two short words are read backwards together

parts.note: am is ante meridiem, in the morning
up means cheerful

explanation.surface: A hunter coming home cheerful in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma, or cougar, is a big cat that stalks prey, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Bride aged badly, hiding old age in a good way

indicators.note: hiding means the rearranged letters conceal the letter for old
badly says these letters are put together wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bride who aged poorly and hides her age, yet somehow aged well.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDE AGED rearranged gives BIDEGRADE, which hides O after BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Biodegrading is decaying naturally without harm to the environment, a benign kind of breaking down over time.

clue.text: Girl's coin the same however you flip it

indicators.text: the same however you flip it
indicators.note: flipping a coin either way shows the same, so the word reads alike in both directions

parts.note: a former Indian coin

explanation.surface: A girl's coin that lands the same whichever way you toss it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Economy: German nation's redeeming feature

parts.note: saving is economy, thrift
a race is a nation or people; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A German nation whose thrift is its one good quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving grace is the one good quality that redeems an otherwise faulty person or thing.

clue.text: Step back in disgust out of cow's droppings

indicators.note: out of means that letter is taken from the droppings

parts.note: cowpats are cow's droppings, so pats

indicators.note: back in points to the last letter of disgust

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stepping back in disgust out of a cowpat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step back' looks like a reversal, but 'Step' is the definition and 'back in disgust' gives the final T, which comes out of PATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pas is the French word for step, used in English for a dance step such as pas de deux.

clue.text: Daughter left covered with unfortunately oily soap

indicators.note: covered with means the letter for left is wrapped by the word for unfortunately

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A daughter left to wallow in some unfortunately greasy soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Dallas was the 1980s American TV soap opera about the Ewing oil family.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas was a soap opera centred on a Texas oil dynasty, so oily describes its subject.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation's insulation is disappointing

parts.note: a let is a rented, temporary home; with 's it becomes lets
down, soft feathers, is used to insulate duvets and jackets

explanation.surface: A rented flat's poor insulation proves a let-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone down is to fail them, which is disappointing, so the phrasal verb fits.
